topic: Ocean Drive and cars: an on-again, off-again relationship. Angle: the history of Ocean Drive flipping between car-free and cars, and what a car-free winter would look like if you go. Facts to use: In September 2026 Miami Beach commissioners voted 7-0 to ask Miami-Dade County to close the 10-block stretch of Ocean Drive between 5th and 15th streets (Lummus Park side, hotels and sidewalk cafes) to cars from Thanksgiving through March 31 every year. The original proposal reopened it after Valentine's Day; commissioners extended it through March to cover spring break. Miami-Dade County and FDOT still have to review and permit it. History: Ocean Drive closed to cars in 2020 during the pandemic for outdoor dining and distancing; it reopened to cars on January 24, 2022 after nearly two years (NBC 6, Miami Herald); in February 2025 Miami Beach reopened it to two-way traffic and removed the bike lanes (WLRN); the city has since tried partial closures for events like the World Cup. Businesses are divided: some say closing it helps foot traffic, others say it hurts hotel access and pushes congestion onto parallel streets. Slides: the news (7-0 vote, dates, stretch), the flip-flop timeline 2020 to 2022 to 2025 to 2026, what changes for you this winter (walkable, bike-friendly, no cruising), the debate, what happens next (county/FDOT). Photos: striking photos of Ocean Drive, South Beach art deco hotels and neon at night, Lummus Park, crowds walking the street; stock or AI. Do not use or mention other Instagram accounts. End with a question: would you rather walk it or drive it?
